findings.title: The public-input guard lets separator-joined and unseparated recovery phrases through as DPNS names
findings.affected: `packages/secret-boundary/src/public-input-guard.ts`; Activity Viewer and watch-only Discovery Scanner, both editions.
findings.reproduction: Enter the public test phrase `zoo … wrong` joined by hyphens, written without separators, or one word per line with a wrong last word, in single or batch input (`public-input-guard.audit.test.ts`).
findings.expected: Any input that is a recovery phrase in a recognisable form is refused locally before any provider is chosen.
findings.observed: Three of 25 forms were accepted as DPNS identity names. Spaces, case, line breaks, commas, dots and underscores were refused.
findings.impact: The Identity lookup would have sent the phrase to the Platform provider. About 37.8 % of random 12-word phrases written without spaces, and 0.18 % joined by hyphens, fit a DPNS label (`dpns-length-fraction`, local). Prerequisite: the person types their own phrase into a public-data tool in one of these forms. No request was made by the probe.
findings.evidence: Harness 3 of 25 failed at the reviewed commit, 25 of 25 passed after the fix; `packages/secret-boundary/tests/public-input-guard.test.ts`.
findings.recommendedFix: Split at every separator and also try cutting unseparated text into BIP39 words; refuse twelve words of one list in a row in a batch regardless of the checksum.
findings.requiredVerification: All 26 forms are refused in single and batch input; ordinary DPNS names still pass.

findings.title: Chosen-words generation accepts a random source that returns too few bytes
findings.reproduction: Inject a random source that returns one byte fewer than requested and generate 2,000 phrases (`chosen-words.audit.test.ts`).
findings.expected: A source of the wrong length or type is refused, as the SLIP-39 share generator does.
findings.observed: 3 of 2,000 phrases had an invalid BIP39 checksum.
findings.impact: Not reachable from the page, which always uses `crypto.getRandomValues`; the option exists for tests and the startup self-test. The output distribution with a correct source passed the chi-square probes.
findings.evidence: Harness 1 of 4 failed at the reviewed commit; after the fix 2,000 of 2,000 short-source calls are refused (`chosen-words-probe-fixed.json`, local); `bip39-chosen-words.test.ts`.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a `Uint8Array` of exactly the requested length; wipe and refuse anything else.
findings.requiredVerification: Short and wrong-type sources are refused; valid sources give the same phrases as before.

findings.title: SSKR encoding check accepts Object.prototype names
findings.reproduction: Call share creation or recovery with the encoding `toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__` or `hasOwnProperty`.
findings.expected: Only the two supported encodings are accepted (the contract restored for AUD-017-API001).
findings.observed: The names found inherited values, passed the check, and the WASM side read them as Compact UR.
findings.impact: The page always passes one of its two option values, so no page output was affected. A library caller could get a format other than the one it named.
findings.evidence: 8 of 16 previous-finding probes failed at the reviewed commit; all pass after the fix; `packages/recovery-backup/tests/sskr.test.ts`.
findings.requiredVerification: The four names are refused for creation and recovery.

findings.title: Platform Explorer no longer serves the address-history route the tools call
findings.affected: `packages/dash-network/src/platform-address-history.ts:160` (Activity Viewer Platform address history); `apps/discovery-scanner/src/dash-platform-network.ts:256` and `:260` (first and last use of a Platform address in the Scanner); both editions, mainnet and testnet.
findings.reproduction: `pnpm test:activity-viewer:platform-testnet`, or request `/platformAddress/<address>/transactions?page=1&limit=2&order=desc` from either Explorer endpoint for the public fixture addresses of the smoke script.
findings.expected: The provider returns the address's transitions, which the Viewer validates and shows and the Scanner uses for first and last use.
findings.observed: HTTP 404 with "Route GET:/platformAddress/…/transactions… not found" on testnet and mainnet. `/info` answers 200, and `/platformAddress/<address>/transitions` answers 200 with a `resultSet` of transitions. The baseline smoke on 2026-10-01 at 12:56 UTC failed the same way, and so did the repeat at the verification commit.
findings.impact: Platform address history in the Activity Viewer fails for every address with transitions, and the Scanner cannot date a used Platform address. No secret is involved; the tools fail closed with a provider error. The cause is a change at the provider, not in this repository; the Discovery testnet smoke passed because it did not reach this route.
findings.evidence: Live smoke logs and route probes (local). After the fix: 124 tests in 15 files, of which 5 fail when the old route is restored; `pnpm test:activity-viewer:platform-testnet` and `-mainnet` pass; a live probe of the Scanner path dates first and last use on both networks.
findings.recommendedFix: Move both callers to the `/transitions` route after checking that its pagination and item fields match what `validateAddressHistoryPage`, `transitionView` and `platformPageTimestamp` expect; make the test fetchers answer only the provider's real routes, which is why no test noticed.
findings.requiredVerification: Both Platform live smokes (Viewer testnet and mainnet) pass; unit tests with a recorded `/transitions` page; artifact gates accept the new route.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A supported Activity Viewer feature fails on both networks in the published v0.1.5-rc.1; the final v0.1.5 must contain the fix.

findings.title: The weekly upstream check stopped reading its source pins after the double-quote reformat
findings.reproduction: Run `node tooling/upstream-version-check.mjs` at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Every pin is read locally and compared with its upstream.
findings.observed: The SLIP-39 and SeedQR commits were read with a single-quote pattern; after the reformat the check stopped with "Cannot read the pinned slip39-reference source commit" and compared nothing. Its malformed-response test passed anyway because it expected only the failure status.
findings.impact: Every scheduled run reported a checker failure; upstream releases and advisories went unnoticed. The format-only harness lists `tooling/verify-project-facts.mjs` and two other scripts as adjusted in the reformat, but not this one.
findings.evidence: Source reading; `upstream-version-check.test.mjs` (9 tests with the launcher tooling test at the verification commit).
findings.recommendedFix: Import the pin list instead of parsing the file; test that every local pin is read; require the parse error itself in the malformed-response test.
findings.requiredVerification: The check reads every pin without a request; the tests fail if the pin list cannot be read.

findings.title: The release workflow grants write, OIDC and attestation permissions to every job
findings.reproduction: Read the workflow-level `permissions` block at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Read-only by default; only the publishing job, which runs no installed dependency, may write, request an OIDC token and attest.
findings.observed: `contents: write`, `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` applied to the browser and build jobs, which install and run locked dependencies.
findings.impact: Code in a compromised locked dependency could have used the write token or signed a provenance attestation under this workflow's identity. No compromise was observed.
findings.evidence: Workflow source; tag run of v0.1.5-rc.1 passed with the narrowed permissions.
findings.recommendedFix: Workflow-level `contents: read`; grant the three permissions to the publish job only.
findings.requiredVerification: A tag run publishes with attestations while the other jobs are read-only.

findings.title: RustSec does not audit the executable Deriver's Cargo.lock
findings.reproduction: Read the lockfile list and path filters of the RustSec workflow.
findings.expected: Every shipped native or WASM crate set is audited.
findings.observed: Only the four WASM lockfiles were audited, and the launcher was outside the path filters.
findings.impact: An advisory against a launcher crate would not have been reported. The local cargo audit of that lockfile found none on 2026-10-01.
findings.evidence: `cargo-audit-apps-key-derivation-launcher` (local), 10 crates, no advisory; RustSec run at fce5a3b passed.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the lockfile and the launcher paths.

findings.title: The release publishes executables that no job of the tag run started
findings.reproduction: Read the tag workflow at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Each published executable is run against the canonical page before publishing.
findings.observed: Linux, Windows and macOS executables were built and published without being started; only `launchers.yml` on `main` ran them, and only when its path filter matched.
findings.impact: A release could ship an executable that had never run for that commit.
findings.evidence: Workflow source; the v0.1.5-rc.1 tag run included the new launchers job and passed.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a job that runs `tooling/verify-key-derivation-launcher.mjs` on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS and make publishing wait for it.
findings.requiredVerification: A tag run with the job passes and publish depends on it.

findings.title: A phrase made with chosen words is not offered to the backup tabs
findings.reproduction: From an empty phrase field, generate with chosen words and open a Recover & Back Up tab.
findings.expected: "Import from Generate & Derive" is offered, as after an ordinary generation.
findings.observed: The offer was queued as a microtask before the asynchronous search had filled the field, so it was made for the previous (empty) content.
findings.impact: A convenience was missing; "Use in Recover & Back Up" still worked.
findings.recommendedFix: Offer the phrase again once it is in the field.
findings.requiredVerification: Controller test with the chosen-words path.

findings.title: Mode tabs shrink below their longest word between the phone and desktop layouts
findings.expected: Tabs keep the width of their longest word and wrap into another row.
findings.observed: At 640 px with Child seeds shown, the Dash Community tab had 75 px of content in 70 px.
findings.impact: Clipped tab text at one width range.
findings.evidence: `baseline-check-layout-extra-widths` and screenshots `deriver-dash-community-640-*` (local); no finding at six widths after the fix.
findings.recommendedFix: A minimum width of the longest word and wrapping rows in the three style sheets.

findings.title: Build and verification documents describe an earlier WASM, source and release set
findings.reproduction: Compare the documents with the canonical manifest and the release workflow.
findings.expected: Four rebuilt WASM modules; MHFE as a vendored package; MnemoCode and MHFE among the hashed sources; executables and legal files in the release.
findings.observed: Five rebuilt modules; incomplete hashed-source lists; a release description without executables, verification record and legal files; an outdated description of the upstream check.
findings.impact: A reviewer following the documents would expect a different build.
findings.requiredVerification: pnpm metadata:check and a reading against the manifests.

findings.title: The security documents omit the executable Deriver and chosen-words generation
findings.reproduction: Read the documents against the shipped features.
findings.expected: A native program that opens a local port, and a generator that lowers phrase strength by design, are described with their limits.
findings.impact: Users and reviewers could not assess the local server or the weakened phrases from the security documents.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe what the executable serves and to whom, its headers, limits and Host check, and how chosen words draw, warn and refuse.

findings.title: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md omits the crates and runtime of the executable Deriver
findings.expected: Every crate compiled into a published binary, and the Rust standard library, is listed.
findings.observed: Six launcher crates and the Rust runtime were missing although the file called its list complete; the policy section also counted seven MHFE files instead of six and left MnemoCode out of the hashed sources.
findings.impact: Incomplete license attribution for the published executables.
findings.recommendedFix: A launcher section with crates, runtime and linkers; correct counts.
findings.requiredVerification: Every launcher lockfile crate appears in the notices.

findings.title: Two copies of the host-platform mapping for building and checking executables
findings.expected: One mapping from this computer to a launcher platform.
findings.observed: Each script had its own copy with different error messages.
findings.impact: A change to one copy would make the check look for another file than the build writes.
findings.recommendedFix: Export one `hostPlatform()` and use it in both.
findings.requiredVerification: The new test of the mapping and file names.

findings.title: A failing layout self-test leaves its temporary directory behind
findings.reproduction: Make the self-test fail and look in the temporary directory.
findings.expected: The temporary page is removed in every case.
findings.observed: `process.exit(1)` inside the `try` skipped the `finally`; two such directories from earlier runs remained.
findings.impact: Disk clutter only; the page holds no secret.
findings.recommendedFix: Set the exit code and return.
findings.requiredVerification: Self-test passes and leaves no directory.

informationalNotes: The formatting range 8880e9e..062e907 changes 600 files; 593 are only reformatted and the seven others are the declared configuration and script adjustments. The scripts that parsed source text were adjusted except `tooling/upstream-version-check.mjs` (AUD-019-BLD001).

cargo audit reports allowed warnings: `paste` is unmaintained (RUSTSEC-2024-0436) in the SSKR and Gordian Envelope crates, `atomic-polyfill` is unmaintained (RUSTSEC-2023-0089) in the Orchard crate, and `yoke-derive` 0.8.3 is yanked in the Gordian Envelope lockfile. None is a vulnerability; they are recorded for the next dependency update.
Private vulnerability reporting is enabled for the public repository (read through the GitHub API).

The MHFE browser package changed after the reviewed commit (3fdb1fdfdb4611397f14317e1307b9897671a806, MHFE 0.4.0 release at e1c0c8f1e70246e49cac3d0510f6ce6c758c4d6e). Its bytes match the release's SHA256SUMS; this audit reviewed its integration through the reduced-cost vector only, not the MHFE implementation, which has its own audits in hobby-eng/mhfe.

Fix from AUD-017; replayed by the previous-findings harness.

limitations: The review ran in two phases. The first phase (baseline, probes and remediation) ended when the session crashed; its working notes were lost. The findings above are taken from the retained evidence, the harnesses and the remediation commit messages, which name each finding ID. The second phase restored the snapshot and ledger, re-verified the fixes at 3fdb1fdfdb4611397f14317e1307b9897671a806, found and fixed AUD-019-API003 while rechecking the failed live smoke, and wrote this record.

Many coverage rows rest on the repository's automated suites (pnpm verify, vectors, browser suites, matrix smoke) rather than on new manual differential work; the ledger says so per row. No live Core regtest comparison, mainnet smoke, uncached canonical Docker build, or macOS and Windows executable run was done locally; CI ran the canonical build and the executables at fce5a3b.
The reviewer of both phases also wrote the fixes; no second reviewer checked them. The fix of AUD-019-API003 is a local commit not yet checked by CI. This is not a security certification.

privacyProvenance.note: Owner-authorized privacy-only publication metadata; no audit checks were rerun. Original instants, date precision, findings, counts, source and artifact hashes, and raw local evidence are retained. Date-only records gain no inferred clock value. Original document bindings remain recorded as historical provenance; current document bindings identify publication bytes only.
